diagnosis: Acute gout flare of the right big toe. Your uric acid level was 9.1 mg/dL.
hospital_course: You came to the emergency department with sudden severe pain, redness, and swelling in your right big toe. Fluid taken from the joint showed uric acid crystals and no infection. You were treated with colchicine and your pain has improved. You are walking with mild discomfort.

medications.name: Colchicine
medications.note: Stop and call us if you have diarrhea.

medications.name: Naproxen
medications.frequency: every 12 hours as needed for pain

diet: You should drink at least 2 liters of water a day.
Please avoid beer and liquor, and limit wine to one glass on any day.
Avoid organ meats such as liver and kidney, and shellfish such as shrimp and mussels.
Limit red meat to one small serving a day.
Avoid sodas and juices sweetened with high-fructose corn syrup.
Low-fat dairy foods such as milk and yogurt are fine.
activity: Rest and raise your right foot when you can for the next 3 days.
You may walk as pain allows, and return to normal activity when the swelling is gone.
care: Put an ice pack wrapped in a towel on the toe for 20 minutes, three times a day.
Wear loose, soft shoes or sandals until the swelling goes down.
monitoring: Write down your toe pain on a 0 to 10 scale every evening for 7 days.

follow_up.purpose: a pain check and to discuss allopurinol
a repeat uric acid and kidney blood test

warning_signs: a fever of 101 F (38.3 C) or higher with chills
red streaks spreading up your foot or leg
chest pain, trouble breathing, or fainting
call_clinic: your pain is not better after 3 days
you have diarrhea, vomiting, or black stools
